digest.component_or_area: LLM model configuration and deprecation registry
propositions: REBAR_LLM_MODEL must be registered as a scheduled (removable) deprecation in _deprecations.REGISTRY with remove_in=_MAJOR, not as a permanent alias, because it is superseded by a different interface (per-class slots) rather than merely renamed.

The deprecation warning must be emitted at both env-read sites (config.py:469 and model_classes.py) with full provenance, never at resolve_model_string where provenance is lost, to correctly distinguish deprecated env-var sources from config-table or per-step model specifications.
When REBAR_LLM_MODEL is set and no classes are explicitly configured, it must map to all three model classes as the widest-compatibility fallback during the migration window.

User-facing strings and documentation presenting REBAR_LLM_MODEL as the current model-selection interface (including project README.md, CLI help text, MCP tool descriptions, and five other prose files) must be retargeted to present the class-based configuration as primary and mark the env var as deprecated.

The warning is emitted per call (not once-per-process) whenever REBAR_LLM_MODEL is consulted, including when CLI flags override it, so operators are alerted to the deprecated export regardless of what runs first.
Example configurations for each provider (Anthropic-only, Bedrock-only, mixed-provider, local+fallback) must be shipped in docs as complete copy-paste-ready [tool.rebar.llm.model_classes] tables.
